title: German test sites check IdentiFlight cameras that detect eagles and signal wind turbines to slow
summary: IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at a German test site in 2025; no German source measures a drop in bird deaths.
account: OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with observations by ornithologists at German test sites. OekoFor's dated updates report that the red-kite validation was completed in October 2021. The OECD AI Incidents entry summarizes press coverage of 20 and 21 September 2022 (The Guardian, Mother Jones, The Register and others, not among the sources). It says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight to detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines and slow the blades to prevent collisions. The monitor's rationale cites the 82% reduction reported from the Wyoming study. It cites no German measurement. OekoFor's updates report the publication of a white-tailed eagle assessment in May 2023. These updates give no estimate of any reduction in bird deaths in Germany. They also give no start date for the lesser spotted eagle tests. Two U.S. Geological Survey scientists argued in 2023 that the Wyoming data show little evidence of fewer eagle deaths. The Bavarian state environment office reported 31 dangerous red kite flights through rotors at a forest site since spring 2024 and no observed collisions. On 27 August 2026, OekoFor and ARSU reported for Boulder Imaging that IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at Kublank in 2025. On 27 October 2026, the competence center KNE (Kompetenzzentrum Naturschutz und Energiewende) listed basic recognition of V5 for red kite, black kite, white-tailed eagle and lesser spotted eagle classification.
purpose: IdentiFlight is built to detect eagles and curtail turbines. Its intended use in Germany is to protect lesser spotted eagles at wind farms.
system: IdentiFlight automated eagle detection and turbine curtailment

The authors measure detection, classification and shutdown signals against ornithologists' reference data at three sites in 2025, and they do not count bird deaths.

display.answer: OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with ornithologists' observations. Boulder Imaging, the maker of IdentiFlight, commissioned their report of 27 August 2026. The recognition by the competence center KNE rests on test reports that the system makers commissioned. The OECD entry summarizes press coverage of September 2022 and cites the Wyoming estimate that two U.S. Geological Survey scientists disputed in 2023.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at a German test site in 2025; no German source measures a drop in bird deaths.
fields.account: OekoFor and ARSU compare camera detections with observations by ornithologists at German test sites. OekoFor's dated updates report that the red-kite validation was completed in October 2021. The OECD AI Incidents entry summarizes press coverage of 20 and 21 September 2022 (The Guardian, Mother Jones, The Register and others, not among the sources). It says that Germany is deploying AI-powered camera systems developed by IdentiFlight to detect endangered lesser spotted eagles near wind turbines and slow the blades to prevent collisions. The monitor's rationale cites the 82% reduction reported from the Wyoming study. It cites no German measurement. OekoFor's updates report the publication of a white-tailed eagle assessment in May 2023. These updates give no estimate of any reduction in bird deaths in Germany. They also give no start date for the lesser spotted eagle tests. Two U.S. Geological Survey scientists argued in 2023 that the Wyoming data show little evidence of fewer eagle deaths. The Bavarian state environment office reported 31 dangerous red kite flights through rotors at a forest site since spring 2024 and no observed collisions. On 27 August 2026, OekoFor and ARSU reported for Boulder Imaging that IdentiFlight V5 classified lesser spotted eagles correctly in 97.8% of checked images at Kublank in 2025. On 27 October 2026, the competence center KNE (Kompetenzzentrum Naturschutz und Energiewende) listed basic recognition of V5 for red kite, black kite, white-tailed eagle and lesser spotted eagle classification.
